correctness.rationale: For each n>=2 and 1<=d<n, inverse a rotates set and crossing indices, while inverse b changes only bit 0 to bit d. A pre-first-growth inverse b step is neutral or shrinks: when shrinking, it destroys but cannot create any directed 0-to-1 crossing on d-edges. Therefore >=min E a-steps before the first growing b, and inverse a^r then b attains 1+r. If E empty, each d-orbit has constant membership, so inverse b cannot act and extension is impossible. For gcd(n,d)=1 all d-edges form one directed cycle; suppressing t consecutive-start edges gives a vertex-disjoint directed-path forest (for t<n) and counting nonincreasing 1...10...0 occupancy on each path gives product A_t; differences give all multiplicities. For t=n-1 a spanning directed path has n+1 allowable labelings; only two are trivial, giving exactly n-1 hardest proper subsets. Tested exact inverse BFS against every subset for 45 automata (n=2..10, all d), 16298 instances, including noncoprime cases, and independent forest-product counts.

value.rationale: Complete classification of a natural shortest preimage-extension invariant explicitly motivating new 2026 automata literature, for all cyclic-copy parameters. Provides an exact computable full distribution, sharp maximal length, exactly one exceptional subset per cardinality, and exponentially small hard proportion, with genuine displacement-dependent spectra. The global upper bound alone or a single worst example would not establish these structural facts; the invariant is central to subset extension methods, not arbitrary finite data.
